name: Great Barrier Reef
summary: World's largest coral reef ecosystem threatened by back-to-back marine heatwaves, ocean acidification, and severe tropical cyclones.

hotspots.title: Northern Ribbon Coral Formations
hotspots.description: Outer barrier reef crests exposed to surging sea surface temperatures and cyclonic wave action.
hotspots.impactCarryOn: Recurrent 95%+ bleaching events exhaust coral regenerative capacity, leaving dead rubble fields.
hotspots.impactProtect: Thermally resilient coral larval seeding and assisted gene flow accelerate thermal tolerance.

hotspots.title: Central Inshore Lagoon
hotspots.description: Tourism hub sensitive to agricultural sediment plumes, nitrogen runoff, and turbidity.
hotspots.impactCarryOn: Chronic crown-of-thorns starfish outbreaks combined with cloudy sediment stifle calcification.
hotspots.impactProtect: Catchment catchment filtration, automated solar-powered surface shade misters, and water quality reform.

hotspots.title: Southern Coral Cays & Turtle Rookeries
hotspots.description: Low-lying sand cays critical for green turtle and pelagic seabird nesting.
hotspots.impactCarryOn: Erosion from sea level rise and warming sand temps skew turtle sex ratios to 99% female.
hotspots.impactProtect: Dynamic dune nourishment, artificial nesting shade canopies, and reef flat stabilization.

stats.label: Hard Coral Cover
stats.context: Average live hard coral cover across the 2,300 km reef complex.

stats.label: Marine Heatwave Days/Yr
stats.context: Annual days where ocean temperatures exceed the 90th local percentile threshold.

stats.label: Surface Ocean pH
stats.context: Ocean acidity level (lower pH severely impairs calcium carbonate shell and reef building).

stats.label: Ecosystem Services Value
stats.context: Annual economic and tourism value generated by healthy marine biodiversity.

carryOn.description: Thermal thresholds exceeded continuously, collapsing the 3D carbonate structure into an algal-dominated wasteland.
keyPoints: Over 99% of warm-water coral reefs lost globally
Collapse of marine habitat supporting 1,500 fish species
Loss of natural breakwater exposing coastline to massive storm erosion

protect.description: Limiting peak warming to 1.5°C coupled with genetic adaptation breeding enables resilient coral strains to flourish.
keyPoints: 400+ targeted reef sites seeded with heat-selected micro-fragments
Strict catchment runoff controls eliminating nutrient pollution
Global carbon stabilization preserves ocean carbonate saturation
